title.narrative: NP Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Improvement Project

description.narrative: The development objectives of the Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Improvement Project for Nepal are to: (i) increase sustainable access to improved water services and promote improved sanitation and hygiene practices in rural areas; and (ii) develop and implement a long-term support mechanism to promote the sustainability of water supply schemes in selected districts. The project comprises of four components. The first component, access to improved water supply and sanitation and promotion of improved sanitation and hygiene practices will finance carrying out a program of selection, development, and implementation of schemes. The second component, district level institutional strengthening will promote the long term sustainability of schemes in selected districts through enhancing institutional arrangements and strengthening linkages among key agencies during planning, implementation, and post construction of such schemes. The third component, technical assistance and capacity building, and project management will finance incremental project management and administration costs for components one and two, as well as a variety of financial and safeguards audits, miscellaneous capacity building activities, and sector studies. The fourth component, contingency emergency response will draw resources from the unallocated expenditure category and or enable the government to request the Bank to re-categorize and reallocate financing from other project components to partially cover emergency response and recovery costs.

The development objectives of the project are to: (i) Increase sustainable access to improved water services and promote improved sanitation and hygiene practices in rural areas; and (ii) Develop and implement a long-term support mechanism to promote the sustainability of water supply schemes in selected districts.

title.narrative: Number of VDCs declared ODF by the Districts.

comment.narrative: <p>100 percent of the revised target was achieved. After the 2018 restructuring, the target was revised from 400 to 130 to concentrate only on those VDCs not covered by the Government's sanitation program. During MTR (2017), it was assessed that over half of the VDCs earlier selected under the project had already achieved ODF due to the Government's ambitious target and programs to declare Nepal ODF by 2017. Therefore,  the targets were revised to implement activities on the VDCs that were not yet ODF and to focus on the post-ODF activities to ensure the sustainability of the sanitation and hygiene practices. </p>

Number of people in rural areas provided with access to Improved Water Sources under the project

comment.narrative: <p>The indicator has exceeded its revised target by 10 percent. Original targets were almost reduced to half during the 2018 restructuring as there was a drastic change in way of delivering water to the communities. The original design was to provide water through community standpoints, and the project changed its design to provide water via household connections (yard connections) due to the government's one-house yard policy. This change caused significant cost escalation (around 250 percent), and therefor targets were substantially reduced. After the 2018 restructuring, the design of the Batch 10 schemes was changed to provided water via household connections. Access to water was provided through community taps to 355,325 people (Batch 9 schemes) and through yard connection at the household level to 439,759 people (Batch 10 schemes).</p>

title.narrative: Number of schemes visited by the backstopping facility at the District level; of which (percentage of schemes non-functioning).

comment.narrative: <p>116.51 percent of the revised target was achieved.  Due to federalization, the project changed its design to focus on the municipality instead of the district-level institutional strengthening. Originally, the project had selected five districts (Sunsari, Dolakha, Makwanpur, Lamjung, and Salyan) as pilot districts, however, after the 2018 restructuring and to align with the federalizaion and strengthening of local government to provide water and sanitation services, municipalities were selected as pilot municipalities (instead of the district). This reduced the scope of the project and the number of schemes to be visited at the district was significantly reduced. The original five pilot districts consist of a total of 256 VDCs and Municipalities with 3,670 schemes. After the 2018 restructuring, eight municipalities (in three additional districts  - Dhansuha, Rupandehi, and Kailali) were selected as pilot municipalities. During April 2020 restructuring, the earlier selected eight municipalities were further reduced to six municipalities (and four districts - Sunsari, Dolakha, Lamjung, and Salyan) during April 2020 restructuring. Makwanpur district was dropped from the pilot districts lists.</p>

comment.narrative: The indicator was dropped during 2020 Restructuring. The request letter from GoN dated Nov 12, 2019, for extension of the closing date and amendment of results framework, and no objection letter provided by the Bank ltr dated Dec 10, 2019, shows this indicator was dropped. The Fund Board did not provide hardware support for the construction of the HH toilets and was only involved in the software part. The HH toilets damaged were rehabilitated by the communities with support from other agencies and local NGOs./p>
